newsitem.title: UK: Spanish bonds are the week's victors - Salomon.
newsitem.headline: Spanish bonds are the week's victors - Salomon.

text.p: Spanish bonds outstripped other government bond markets in the week to October 10, while U.S. bonds brought up the rear, Salomon Brothers said on Friday.
The Salomon Brothers world government bond index made total gains for the week of 0.31 percent in local currency terms and 0.37 percent in dollar terms.

As European issues surrounding a European single currency continued to provide a focus for markets, Spain received a boost from the growing belief that it is on target to meet the Maastricht criteria and may be among the founder members of European economic and monetary union in 1999.
Spanish government bonds made gains of 1.06 percent in local currency terms and 1.15 percent in dollars.
Canadian bonds also put in a strong performance gaining 1.00 percent in Canadian dollars and 1.70 percent in U.S. dollars.

With convergence continuing to be an important factor in European bond markets, Finland and Sweden also faired well. Finland gained 0.75 percent in local currency terms and Sweden 0.57 percent. In dollar terms they made 0.56 percent and 0.94 percent gains respecitvely, Salomon's data showed.
Among the major European government bonds France made a respectable 0.70 percent in French francs and 0.84 percent in dollar terms.

Gains for German, British and Italian bonds were less impressive. German bonds made gains of 0.34 percent in local currency terms and 0.40 percent in dollar terms, just ahead of British bonds which showed 0.32 percent gains in sterling and 0.34 percent in dollars.

But Italian bonds, which have seen strong outperformance in recent weeks, could only manage gains of 0.17 percent in local currency terms. The also showed the only deficit of the week with a 0.27 percent loss in dollars.
Further a field, JGBs were in seventh place, making gains of 0.42 percent in yen terms and 0.59 percent in dollars.
At the bottom of the table were U.S. bonds, scraping through with a mere 0.01 percent gain.

Salomon's bond index is calculated using all government bonds with over one year to maturity, weighted for market capitalisation. Only bonds freely available to institutional investors and with a certain minimum amount outstanding are included. Returns take account of price moves and accrued interest.
